sources.entry: Letters - Teach your kids the alphabet and how to type.

summary.one_liner: Letters is a Mac app that teaches young children the alphabet and typing by showing and pronouncing each key they press.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a macOS app for learning typing and the alphabet, written by the author for their two-year-old son who enjoys pressing keys and hearing the letter spoken aloud. The README says the app reacts to typed letters, which the author describes as the child pronouncing the letter he just typed. The README is very brief and does not document specific features, controls, or settings. It has empty "Screen recording" and "Screenshots" sections, so no visuals are provided. Setup and implementation details are not given.
notable: Built by a parent for their own two-year-old child
Focused on typing and alphabet recognition for toddlers
Speaks the letter aloud as it is typed, according to the author's description
caveats: README is minimal; no installation or build instructions are provided
Screen recording and screenshot sections are empty
